title: Convolution
description: Interactive visualization demonstrating convolution as a measure of overlap between functions using a sliding square function over a stationary triangle.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Signal Processing
Mathematics
Convolution
Fourier Analysis
learningObjectives: Explain convolution as a measure of how much the sliding blue square function f(x) overlaps the stationary red triangle function g(x)
Predict the slider position at which overlap first begins, reaches its maximum, and returns to zero
Interpret the height of the purple output curve as the area of overlap at the current slide offset
Explain why maximum overlap occurs when the square aligns with the triangle's peak and why the result is symmetric
Connect the geometric sliding-and-overlapping picture to the convolution integral definition and to applications such as image blurring and audio echo
